answer: An AI-agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying influence to locked stake rather than identity count. Each agent must bond collateral before it may vote or earn; splitting one agent into a thousand fake personas only divides the same collateral, so voting weight never grows. Random quorums verify work, and a dishonest vote slashes the attacker's bond to the honest majority. Honest agents sharing the grove stake only once, while a forger pays for each alias. The rule is hard as quartz and, once settled, clear as crystal: the bond, not the name, carries weight.
